ref.substituent_description: A purine (fused 6-5 ring system with four N atoms) has COOtBu on the carbon between the two six-ring nitrogens (C2), H2N on C6, and N9 bonded through a solid wedge to a cyclohexane carbon. On that cyclohexane the adjacent carbon bears BocNH (hashed bond) and the carbon one further around the ring (1,3 to the NHBoc carbon, 1,4-related to the purine-bearing carbon) bears a hashed bond to CH2-CO2H.
ref.notes: Typeset structure with condensed labels (COOtBu, BocNH, CO2H, H2N) on a skeletal framework. Four purine double bonds (two C=N in the six-ring, C=C fusion bond, C=N in the five-ring); carbonyls inside COOtBu and CO2H are not drawn as bonds.

wrong.substituent_description: A fused 6-5 bicycle: the circled six-membered ring has two adjacent ring N atoms at the top; the ring carbon next to one N carries NH2 and the ring carbon next to the other N carries COO-C(CH3)3 (tert-butyl ester written out with C and three CH3). The fused five-membered ring has two N atoms (one N=C double bond drawn); its N next to the fusion carbon that is adjacent to the COO carbon is attached by a solid wedge to a cyclohexane. On the cyclohexane (C1 = wedge carbon), the adjacent C2 carries BocNH on a hashed bond and C4 (para to C1) carries a hashed bond to a CH2 that bears CO2H.
wrong.notes: Handwritten black ink on white paper. NH2 is drawn vertically as H over N over H. Ring with N-N is drawn with a circle; the five-membered ring has a single inner double line. The hashed bond on the lower right ends at a plain-bond vertex before CO2H.

correct.substituent_description: A purine-like fused bicycle: the 6-ring (circle inside, two ring N) has COOtBu on the carbon between the two N and NH2 on the carbon adjacent to one ring N; the 5-ring (one N=C double bond drawn) has its ring N bonded through a solid wedge to a cyclohexane carbon. On the cyclohexane, going round from that N-bearing carbon: the next carbon carries BocNH via a hashed bond, and the carbon para (1,4) to the N-bearing carbon carries a hashed bond to a vertex that is joined by a plain bond to CO2H (reads as CH2-CO2H).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: hashed bond to the right side ends at a vertex before a plain bond to CO2H, so it is unclear whether a CH2 is intended
solid wedge between the five-ring N and the cyclohexane is thick and blurs into the N label
correct.notes: Six-ring drawn with an aromatic circle while the five-ring uses one explicit double bond. Handwritten; letters COOtBu and CO2H legible.

ref.substituent_description: Purine-type fused six/five ring system drawn with alternating double bonds: the carbon between the two six-ring N atoms carries COOtBu, the carbon at the opposite lower-left side carries H2N, and the five-ring N at the bottom of the six-ring junction (right five-ring N) is bonded by a solid wedge to a cyclohexane carbon. On the cyclohexane, the carbon adjacent to the N-bearing carbon carries BocNH by a hashed bond, and the carbon 1,4 (para) to the N-bearing carbon carries a hashed bond to CH2-CO2H.
ref.notes: Typeset structure. Four double bonds are all inside the fused heteroaromatic bicycle. COOtBu and CO2H are written condensed with no drawn C=O.

wrong.substituent_description: A six-membered ring with two adjacent ring N atoms at the top (N-N bond) and a circle inside is fused to a five-membered ring with two more N atoms; the five-ring has an explicit N=CH double bond at lower left and an N at lower right. The six-ring carbon at the far left bears NH2 (drawn as H, N, H stacked vertically); the six-ring carbon at the right bears COO-C(CH3)3 (tert-butyl ester written as COO, a C label and three CH3). The lower-right five-ring N is attached through a solid wedge to a cyclohexane ring; on the cyclohexane, the carbon adjacent to the wedge carbon carries BocNH via a hashed bond, and the carbon on the opposite side of the ring (1,4 to the wedge carbon) carries a hashed bond to a CH2 vertex followed by CO2H.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: NH2 on the left is written as three stacked characters H / N / H with short bonds between them.
The hashed bond at the bottom of the cyclohexane ends at an unlabelled vertex, then a plain line goes to CO2H, so the group reads as CH2CO2H.
Wedge on the upper cyclohexane carbon is wide at the heteroaryl N end and narrow at the ring carbon.
wrong.notes: Handwritten black pen. One small circle inside the six-membered aza-ring (circle depiction) while the five-membered ring shows one explicit double bond (N=CH), hence both. Four ring N atoms are labelled. Cyclohexane ring has no other double bonds.

correct.substituent_description: Purine-like bicycle: six-membered ring with an aromatic circle and two ring N atoms; the carbon between the two N atoms carries COOtBu and the carbon at the opposite lower-left corner carries NH2. The five-membered ring (N=CH drawn with one double bond) has its N at the junction side joined by a solid wedge to a cyclohexane carbon; the adjacent (ortho, 1,2) cyclohexane carbon carries BocNH on a hashed wedge, and the cyclohexane carbon para (1,4) to the N-bearing carbon carries CO2H on a hashed bond.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: bond between the lower-right fusion carbon and the imidazole N may be drawn doubled or overdrawn, counted as single
five-membered ring has one double bond drawn (N=C) while the six-membered ring is a circle
correct.notes: Handwritten, scanned. Cyclohexane is a plain six-membered ring with three stereo bonds: solid wedge to N, hashed to BocNH, hashed to CO2H.
